chunks: Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'And whoever is given wisdom, he has indeed been given a great deal of good.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The recognition of the Imam and avoiding the major sins upon which Allah has obligated the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Wisdom (Hikmah) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the Quranic 'Hikmah' not merely as intellectual wisdom but as the dual pillars of Ma'rifat al-Imam (recognition of the Imam) and avoidance of Kabair (major sins). This definition underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inseparable link between theological authority and ethical purification, where true wisdom manifests in both correct belief and righteous action.
